title: A verified treadmill scan books zero exercise minutes and can never build a streak
area: treadmill mode / streak / Unlock ceremonies / streaks / walking · state · treadmill
description: A user props their phone, passes the gait scan, sees the confetti and "Unlocked while you walk", walks 40 minutes, and their Analytics shows zero walking minutes and their streak does not advance. `WalkingFake.start` deliberately skips the progress loop for propped placement, and `completeProppedScan` re-issues the lease and sets phase `walking` but also never starts `play()` — so `walkedSeconds`/`writeWalkingProgress` never run, `details()` stays `{steps: 0, walkingSeconds: 0}`, and the RuleDay row for that state rule stays at 0. A state-only day counts as met for the streak only when walking minutes >= 10, so a treadmill-verified day never counts as a met day.

app-next/src/demo/walkingProgress.ts:4-8 — the only writer of walking minutes

proposed_fix: Have `completeProppedScan` start the same progress loop `start()` uses (with `base` recovered from the existing row), so propped minutes accrue exactly like handheld ones. Add a test that a propped scan followed by 12 minutes of clock advance produces a met day in `todayHistory`/`streak`.

title: Treadmill framing-grace expiry drops the user onto a blocked Home with no explanation - the silent shield the spec forbids

description: A user props their phone, the camera cannot frame them, they see "Can't see you / Step into frame" and after 30 seconds the screen simply closes. title: No decision anywhere for what shields do when the subscription lapses
description: When the entitlement becomes `expired` or `billingIssue`, the paywall is presented above the tabs and Home becomes unreachable (MODEL:212-213). In Phase 2 the DeviceActivity monitors registered by P2-T04 keep repeating weekly and the extension keeps re-shielding at every window start with no app process involved. The user is therefore locked out of their chosen apps by an app they can no longer open without paying, and the only escape is deleting ExcerLock. No spec line, decision or Phase 2 task covers this: grep for "revoke", "lapse", "expired" across plans/rebuild returns nothing about shields.
proposed_fix: Decide and write it into 01-product-model.md §3, then implement in P2-T04: either (a) an unentitled app clears all shields and stops/unregisters every DeviceActivity monitor on the transition into expired/billingIssue, or (b) shields persist but the paywall gains an always-available "Turn blocking off" escape that clears shields without a purchase.
questions_for_johan: When a user's subscription expires or hits a billing issue, should ExcerLock immediately clear all shields and unregister the OS monitors (blocking stops until they pay again), or keep blocking them while the paywall covers the app? If blocking persists, what escape hatch does an unentitled user get to unblock their own apps without paying?
also_titled: Entitlement never reaches the lock machine or the Screen Time port, so lapsing has no defined effect on shields
verifier_note: 01-product-model.md:212-213 and RootNavigator.tsx:28-41 send expired/billingIssue to a hard paywall, while P2-T04:12-15 keeps weekly-repeating DeviceActivity monitors re-shielding from the extension; grep across plans/rebuild for revoke/lapse/expired returns only entitlement mapping (P2-T06:26) and nothing about shields, and app-next/src/domain/resolveLock.ts has no entitlement input. No decision, copy, port contract or task covers shield state on lapse, so the gap is real.

title: Two hardcoded "Test gym unlock" / "Test treadmill unlock" buttons ship on the production Home screen
description: Every user sees two orange secondary buttons labelled "Test gym unlock" and "Test treadmill unlock" between the Lock list row and the Analytics row on Home. Tapping either opens the full-screen unlock ceremony in preview mode (confetti, lock lift, "Done") without any real gym, camera or walking session. In code they are unconditional JSX with English literals hardcoded outside src/content, with no __DEV__ guard and no dev-menu gate. No source in the requirements catalog places any test affordance on Home: the Home content list is StatusCard, ProgressCard per rule, locked-apps row, streak chip and "Add condition".
proposed_fix: Delete both buttons from HomeScreen. The same two ceremonies are already reachable from the dev menu via the unlock-* scenarios (app-next/src/demo/scenarios/unlock.ts) and from the real entry pills inside the lock card, so nothing is lost.
verifier_note: HomeScreen.tsx:254-255 renders two unconditional `SecondaryButton`s with hardcoded English literals 'Test gym unlock' / 'Test treadmill unlock' pushing `/unlock/*?preview=1`, outside src/content and with no guard (no `__DEV__` anywhere in app-next). 02-screen-inventory.md:118-129 lists the required Home content and contains no test affordance.

title: Subscription lapse locks the user out of Settings, account deletion, support and the unlock ceremonies
description: When the entitlement becomes `expired` or `billingIssue` mid-day, `entitled` goes false and the single `Stack.Protected` block containing `(tabs)`, `settings`, `sign-in`, `builder`, `unlock/gym` and `unlock/treadmill` unmounts. The user cannot reach Settings, cannot delete their account (an App Store 5.1.1(v) requirement per `excerlock-app-prd.md:282`), cannot contact support, cannot turn conditions off, and — critically — cannot run the gym or treadmill unlock ceremonies while their apps are still shielded. The spec says the opposite: `plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:97-98` says expired/billingIssue shows the paywall with placement `in_app` **above the tabs**, i.e. the app stays mounted underneath. `PaywallSlot.tsx:35,45` already computes the `in_app` placement and a banner for those two states, but the navigator never lets them render over the tabs.
proposed_fix: Split the gate: keep `(tabs)`/`settings`/`unlock/*` mounted for `expired`/`billingIssue` and present the paywall as a modal above them (placement `in_app`, dismissible back to a read-only/limited app), and reserve the hard unmounting gate for `none`. At minimum, Settings → Account, support and the unlock ceremonies must remain reachable in every non-entitled state.
questions_for_johan: When a subscription lapses while apps are shielded: do the blocked apps unlock immediately (we stop shielding on lapse), stay shielded until the current day's condition is met, or stay shielded indefinitely until the user resubscribes? And which parts of the app stay usable behind the in-app paywall — settings and account only, or also conditions editing?
verifier_note: RootNavigator.tsx:13,34-41 puts (tabs), settings, sign-in, builder and both unlock modals behind one guard requiring status trial/active, so expired/billingIssue unmounts them all, directly contradicting 02-screen-inventory.md:97-98 ("P is shown with placement `in_app` … above the tabs") which PaywallSlot.tsx:35,45 already computes. Account deletion, required in-app per excerlock-app-prd.md:279-282, becomes unreachable in that state.

title: Per-rule progress cards are silently discarded on any locked day that includes a gym or treadmill rule

description: On a locked day with a gym rule or a treadmill/either walking-state rule, the user sees the orange lock with an "I'm at the gym" / "I'm using a treadmill" pill and zero progress anywhere: no step count, no minutes, no bars. title: "Instant relief on gym arrival" has no mechanism in the domain model, the port, or Phase 2
description: The user walks into their gym and their apps stay shielded for a full 30 seconds while a ring fills. Both the PRD and the aha spec require the opposite: shields lift the moment arrival is detected, and the 30-second confirmation only books the reward. Nothing implements it. `LockDecision` has no "arrived, unconfirmed" state, `resolveLock` only unlocks on a `met` RuleDay, and `GymFake.checkIn` writes progress only after the confirmation promise resolves at 30 s. The aha spec's own line "Shields are already lifted by instant-relief; this ring is the reward booking" describes a mechanism that exists nowhere, and P2-T04 never mentions arrival.
evidence: app-next/src/features/unlock/useGymUnlock.ts:91 — credit only on the resolved request
app-next/src/demo/fakes/GymFake.ts:59-67 — setTimeout(confirmation.milliseconds) races presence loss and abort before resolving
docs/specs/aha-unlock-screens.md:190-192 — 'Shields are already lifted by instant-relief; this ring is the reward booking'
proposed_fix: Add a seventh `LockDecision` state (e.g. `unlockedProvisional { ruleId, expiresAt }`) fed by an unconfirmed arrival, ranked above `locked` and below `unlockedWalking`, with a short expiry equal to the confirmation window; `applyLock` clears shields for it, and a failed confirmation simply lets it lapse ("shields simply return — no punishment", PRD:191). Add it to 01-product-model.md §3 and to P2-T04's applyLock table.
also_titled: No instant relief on gym arrival — nothing is credited until the 30-second ring completes
verifier_note: excerlock-app-prd.md:191 locks instant relief "always on, no setting" and docs/specs/aha-unlock-screens.md:191 asserts "Shields are already lifted by instant-relief", yet the LockDecision union (plans/rebuild/01-product-model.md:93-99, domain/resolveLock.ts:16-32) has no provisional state, GymPort.ts:4-15 no arrival surface, and a grep of plans/ for "instant relief" returns nothing — P2-T04 and P2-T05 never mention it. Severity is high rather than blocker: the failure mode is a 30 s wait, not a broken product.

title: No past day is ever recorded — streaks are fixture-only and reset on relaunch
description: A user who meets their condition today, closes the app and reopens it tomorrow has no record of today. Both history writers only ever recompute today's row, past days come entirely from the scenario fixture, and persistence deliberately restores history from the scenario rather than from what the user did. Streaks, the analytics period and the 'days met' figure are therefore theatre with no code path that could survive Phase 2.
evidence: app-next/src/state/todayHistory.ts:12-35 — writes only the row for today
plans/rebuild/01-product-model.md:177-178 — a missed scheduled day breaks the streak
app-next/src/domain/streak.ts:12-21 — iterates rows with d.day <= today && d.scheduled; absent days are invisible
app-next/src/state/todayHistory.ts:12-35 — no row is created for a day the app was not opened
proposed_fix: Persist the day-fact history alongside the rest of the demo context and seal a day's row at rollover (a pure domain function that takes yesterday's progress and writes the final row). Phase 2 then syncs sealed rows rather than inventing history.
also_titled: A missed scheduled day never breaks the streak because no row is written for it

But per-rule met facts do persist (ruleDaysStore.ts:4-8 is a persisted store), so "no past day is ever recorded" overstates it; the gap is the day-fact/history layer, not all history.

title: Enforcement is anchored to a React hook inside the Home tab, so it stops whenever Home is unmounted
description: P2-T04 step 3 wires `applyLock` to `useLockDecision()`. That hook lives in `src/state/selectors.ts` and its only consumer is `HomeScreen`, which is inside the `(tabs)` stack guarded by `entitled && setupComplete`. So enforcement does not run during onboarding, during the post-purchase setup sequence, while the paywall is presented over the tabs after an entitlement lapse, while the app is backgrounded, or after the app is killed. The same defect already exists for progress: `startProgressSync` is mounted in the tabs layout only, so no step or workout progress accrues unless the tab stack is alive. The user's experience is that blocking state is only correct while they are standing on the Home screen.
proposed_fix: Move both the lock-enforcement effect and `startProgressSync` out of the tab tree into the app root (`app/_layout.tsx` / `AppRuntimeProvider`), above every route guard, and add an `AppState` 'active' handler that re-reads permissions, re-runs progress claim-on-open and re-applies the lock. Rewrite P2-T04:36 to name the root, not `useLockDecision()`.
verifier_note: Real placement fragility: `useLockDecision` is consumed only by app-next/src/features/home/HomeScreen.tsx:42 and ShieldPreview, and `startProgressSync` is mounted only in app-next/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx:12, while P2-T04:36 names that hook as the applyLock anchor. But the background/killed claim is wrong — plans/rebuild/phase-2-backend/P2-T04-lock-policy-on-screen-time.md:12-15 registers repeating DeviceActivity schedules that re-shield "without the app running", and P2-T05:7-10,48 already plans foreground/claim-on-open progress, so this is a design-placement defect, not a total enforcement outage.

title: The /dev route is registered with no build guard, and Home accepts unguarded runtime-mutating deep-link params
area: enforcement / Navigation / dev surfaces / Entitlement gating / dev tools
description: Anyone who opens excerlock://dev reaches the full dev menu: a scenario loader for all 32 fixtures, clock skipping (+1 hour / +1 day / set arbitrary ISO time), "Add 1,000 steps", "Pause all conditions", entitlement and session overrides including a fake Apple sign-in, and permission-outcome cyclers. title: The gym time-target ceremony celebrates an unlock that never happens
area: unlock/gym / Unlock ceremonies / gym / gym · minutes target
description: User experience: with a "Spend 30 minutes at the gym" condition, the user arrives, taps "I'm at the gym", holds still for the 30-second ring, and gets the full ceremony — the shackle lifts, confetti fires, a success haptic plays and the screen says "Location detected at the gym / Your gym time is counting". They tap Done, land on Home, and the card still says "Apps are blocked". Nothing on either screen explains that the apps are still locked or that they must stay another 30 minutes. What the code says: for a `target` gym rule `GymFake.checkIn` passes the row's existing progress straight through to `applyProgress`, so `met` stays false and `resolveLock` still returns `locked`. Minutes only accrue afterwards on clock ticks in `gymProgress`. The AHA spec assumes an "instant relief" shield lift on arrival (aha-unlock-screens.md:191, PRD:191) that `resolveLock` has no concept of.
evidence: app-next/src/features/unlock/GymUnlockScreen.tsx:30-31,83-89 (UnlockLockFrame phase 'lifted' with celebrate; subline 'Your gym time is counting')
docs/specs/aha-unlock-screens.md:194-196 (time-target rules get "Your gym time is counting" — arrival credit only starts the clock)
proposed_fix: Either implement instant relief (add an `unlockedArrived` branch to `resolveLock` that opens the apps while gym presence holds inside a time-target rule's window), or stop dressing the time-target path as an unlock: for `mode.kind === 'target'` keep the ring but suppress the shackle lift, the confetti and the success haptic, and replace the copy with something that states the remaining requirement, e.g. "You're checked in — 30 minutes to go" plus a Home progress line. Either way, the copy must not say or imply the apps opened when `resolveLock` still returns `locked`.
questions_for_johan: For a "spend N minutes at the gym" condition, do the apps unlock the moment arrival is confirmed (PRD:191 "instant relief on arrival", which aha-unlock-screens.md:191 assumes is already implemented), or do they stay locked until the N minutes are actually accrued? The rebuild's resolveLock only knows "met", so instant relief is a new lock state that has to be specified — including what happens if the user leaves after two minutes.

For a "spend N minutes at the gym" rule, the arrival ceremony currently lifts the lock and fires confetti even though the apps stay blocked until the minutes accrue. Should that rule get a different, non-celebratory "your gym time is counting" screen, or should arrival unlock immediately?

For "Spend N minutes at the gym", should arriving play the lock-lift ceremony (it doesn't unlock anything yet), a quieter "your clock is running" confirmation, or should the ceremony fire later, when the minutes goal is actually reached?
also_titled: The gym ceremony celebrates an unlock for a gym-minutes rule that books no credit, leaving Home still blocked
The gym ceremony lifts the lock and fires confetti for a minutes rule that has booked nothing

The copy half of the complaint is refuted: docs/specs/aha-unlock-screens.md:194-196 mandates the distinct subline "Your gym time is counting", which content/unlock.ts:31 and GymUnlockScreen.tsx:30-31 implement.

title: Settings → Restore purchases can destroy a live entitlement and eject the user to the paywall
description: A paying user taps Settings → More settings → Restore purchases out of curiosity. The restore fake resolves to `notFound`, patches the entitlement store to `{status:'none'}`, the RootNavigator guard flips, and the whole app (tabs, settings, conditions, unlock screens) unmounts under them and they land on the hard paywall. Code: `DetailedSettingsScreen.tsx:52-58` calls `runtime.subscription.restore()`; `SubscriptionFake.restore` at `src/demo/fakes/SubscriptionFake.ts:19-28` unconditionally patches the store to `none` when the outcome is not 'restored'; and `src/demo/FakeContext.ts:23` freezes `restoreOutcome` at construction from the *scenario's* starting entitlement, so a user who purchased during this session (scenario `fresh-install`, entitlement `none`) still gets `notFound`. Nothing in the spec says a failed restore may revoke an existing entitlement — `plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:95` lists `restored` and `error` as separate paywall states.
proposed_fix: A restore that finds nothing must be a no-op plus a message; only a restore that returns a *newer/valid* entitlement may write the store. Change `SubscriptionFake.restore` to return the current entitlement untouched on `notFound`, and recompute `restoreOutcome` from the live entitlement store rather than freezing it at scenario construction. Add a test that restores from an `active` entitlement and asserts the user stays inside the app.
also_titled: Restore's destructive path is untested because the test stubs the port
verifier_note: Confirmed in code: SubscriptionFake.ts:19-27 patches the entitlement store to `{status:'none'}` whenever restoreOutcome !== 'restored', FakeContext.ts:23 derives that flag from the scenario's starting entitlement, and RootNavigator.tsx:13,34-41 then unmounts the tabs. Two corrections: `restoreOutcome` is not frozen — DevControls.tsx:86-92 / FakeRuntime.ts:117 expose `setRestoreOutcome` — and this is demo-layer code that P2-T06-adapty.md:16-20 replaces with the real adapter, so it is a Phase 1 fake defect rather than a ship blocker.

title: Paywall has no Terms of Use or Privacy Policy links (App Review 3.1.2 rejection)
description: The purchase screen renders only a plain, non-tappable `c.terms` sentence at `PaywallStandIn.tsx:65-69`. The welcome screen does link both docs (`WelcomeFooter.tsx:32-49`) — the paywall does not. Since the paywall is a hard gate on first launch, the reviewer will see it.

title: With several conditions, names and numbers are never shown together
description: On a locked day the user sees a white 'Conditions' list with the rule names and no progress, and (when it renders at all) a set of progress rows inside the lock card with numbers but no names — ProgressCard in `lock` appearance deliberately drops the title and renders icon + detail only. With three conditions the user reads 'Walk 5,000 steps / Arrive at the gym / Run 20 minutes' in one card and '3,120 / 5,000' '0 / 30 min' in another, with no way to tell which number belongs to which condition beyond guessing from the icon. The Home README asserts the opposite ('the separate duplicate condition list is hidden'), which is false — it always renders when a lock card is showing.
proposed_fix: Delete the duplicate white name list and let the in-lock progress rows carry the rule name (or keep the list and give each row its live progress + met tick). One list, name and number on the same row.
verifier_note: HomeScreen.tsx:188-224 renders the white 'Conditions' name list whenever `scheduleCard && progress.length`, contradicting app-next/src/features/home/README.md:5 ("the separate duplicate condition list is hidden"), while ProgressCard.tsx:41-51 drops the title in `lock` appearance and shows only icon + detail. title: Met state carries into days no condition is scheduled — Home says 'Unlocked for the rest of today' on a free Saturday

title: Editing a met condition's days or window re-locks the apps instantly

title: Overlapping rule windows: the earlier window's DeviceActivity interval end clears shields while another rule is still active
description: With rule A 9:00–12:00 and rule B 10:00–14:00 both unmet, `resolveLock` correctly returns `locked` from 9:00 to 14:00. But P2-T04 registers one DeviceActivity schedule per rule window instance whose `intervalDidEnd` clears shields, and the monitor extension cannot run arithmetic or consult other rules (research: "Extension execution is static … No arithmetic, no compute OS-side"). So at 12:00, with the app closed, A's interval end clears the shields and the user's apps are open for two hours they should have been blocked. Adjacent windows (A 9–12, B 12–15) hit the same problem through callback ordering plus the documented minutes of interval jitter. Decision B5 explicitly allows overlapping rules with no conflict validation, so this configuration is expected, not exotic.

Compute the union of all enabled rules' window instances in the domain (a pure `mergedLockIntervals(rules, from, to, tz)` next to `resolveLock`) and register DeviceActivity schedules for the merged intervals only, so an interval end can only mean "no rule is active". Add this to P2-T04 step 1 and to its schedule-generation tests alongside cross-midnight and all-day.

title: Both shield buttons lead nowhere: no deep-link route, and no collapse when notification permission is missing
description: The primary shield button is "Open ExcerLock" and the secondary is "Keep walking" or "OK". P2-T04 targets `excerlock://` and `excerlock://locked-apps`; there is no `locked-apps` route and no deep-link handler anywhere in `app-next/app/` — only a registered scheme. The research doc records `openApp` as a confirmed no-op and the `openUrl` hack as unreliable (the one red gap), so the fallback is a tap-through notification — which is a third notification type that contradicts P2-T09's "the catalog has exactly two ids", has no copy, and no landing screen. The old app's safeguard for exactly this — collapsing the shield to a single "Close" when notification permission is absent, because otherwise the button has no route home — is not represented in `shieldContent`, which always returns two buttons.
proposed_fix: Decide the notification-count law (either P2-T09 admits a third shield tap-through id or P2-T04 drops the workaround), add a `locked-apps` route plus a `Linking` config in `app/_layout.tsx` that survives the boot gate, and give `shieldContent` a `canNotify` input that collapses to a single Close button when notification permission is absent, ported from app/src/shield/README.md:66-73.
questions_for_johan: P2-T04 needs a shield tap-through notification (Apple's shield cannot launch the app) but P2-T09 mandates exactly two notification ids. Do you want the third notification, or should the shield's primary button simply close and rely on the user opening ExcerLock themselves?
verifier_note: Two legs hold: app-next/src/domain/shieldContent.ts:15 always returns two buttons with no canNotify collapse (the old law is app/src/shield/README.md:66-73), and the notification tap-through in P2-T04:26-27 contradicts locked decision B14 (plans/rebuild/00-decisions.md:35) and the "catalog has exactly two ids" test in P2-T09-notifications.md:16, with no copy for a third. The missing `locked-apps` route is refuted as a gap — P2-T04:26-27 names the URL and its destination, so it is scheduled Phase 2 wiring, and app-next/app/ is an Expo Router tree where `excerlock://` already resolves.

title: No error boundary anywhere; an invalid draft throws at render on the plan summary and shows a blank crash
description: User experience: any render-time throw produces a red screen in development and a blank/white crash with no message in a release build. The most reachable case is the onboarding plan summary and the condition builder's summary step: `PlanSummary` calls `toRule(draft, schedule)` during render, and `toRule` throws whenever `validateRule` finds an issue. The user loses their whole in-progress plan and is given no explanation and no way to recover. What the code says: grep for `ErrorBoundary`, `componentDidCatch`, `getDerivedStateFromError` across `app-next/src` and `app-next/app` returns nothing; no Expo Router route exports an `ErrorBoundary`. There is also no Sentry, so the crash leaves no trace.
proposed_fix: Export an `ErrorBoundary` from `app/_layout.tsx` (Expo Router supports this) rendering a plain recovery screen — a heading, one line of copy, and a "Start over" / "Back" button — with the strings in `src/content/common.ts`. Separately, make `PlanSummary` tolerate an invalid draft: have `toRule` return `{rule|issues}` and render an inline "Something in this plan needs a change" row with an Edit link instead of throwing.
verifier_note: The absence of any error boundary is real — grep for ErrorBoundary/componentDidCatch/getDerivedStateFromError over app-next/src and app-next/app returns nothing. But the claimed reachable throw is not demonstrated: every builder step is gated by builderValid (app-next/src/features/conditions/builderFlow.ts:17-24) and the S3/edit footers are disabled on invalid drafts (ConditionBuilder.tsx:38, useBuilder.ts:55), so toRule at PlanSummary.tsx:21 is not shown to throw in normal use.

title: Analytics is missing four other specified elements: the previous-period delta, the three stat tiles, the estimate baseline and the "no conditions" empty state
description: The Analytics tab shows a Time-reclaimed hero with the subtitle "Compared with your starting screen time", a two-series bar chart, an Exercise tile, a streak tile and two footnote lines. Missing versus spec: (1) the delta line "+N min vs previous period" / "No previous measurement to compare" - copy exists unused; (2) the three StatTiles "Days met - 5 of 5 scheduled", "Current streak", "Longest streak" - days met is now a footnote and longest streak a sub-label, and `daysMet`/`scheduled`/`current`/`longest` copy is unused; (3) the locked-app minutes chart with the dashed starting-estimate line - `UsageChart` supports it but is only mounted inside a per-activity bottom sheet with no `estimate` prop, so the baseline never renders and `analyticsCopy.estimate`, `usage` and `average` are unused; (4) the "no rules" empty state - `noRules`/`noRulesBody` copy is unused, so an account with zero conditions still sees a full charts page. The "measured on N of M days" honesty line survives but was demoted from the hero to a bottom footnote.
proposed_fix: Restore the delta line under the hero, promote days-met/current/longest to StatTiles, pass `estimate={baseline}` to a top-level UsageChart of locked-app minutes, and render the `noRules` EmptyState in place of the charts when `rulesStore.rules` is empty.
also_titled: Analytics dropped its "no conditions" empty state, its comparison delta, and moved the measured-days caveat off the hero
The weekly recap card is absent from Analytics although the decision register explicitly keeps it
verifier_note: Two of the four are clean: the delta line is absent (analyticsCopy.delta/noComparison at content/analytics.ts:9-10 unused) and the noRules empty state is never rendered (content/analytics.ts:29-30 unused; AnalyticsScreen.tsx:78-93 only handles dayZero/noData). But locked-app minutes ARE charted — ComparisonChart.tsx:13-17 plots a "Screen time" series, so only the dashed estimate baseline is missing — and days-met/current/longest are all present, merely demoted from StatTiles to a footnote and sub-label (AnalyticsScreen.tsx:118-131, 150-155).

title: Signing in from the welcome screen does nothing — no restore, no entitlement check, no skip
description: 'Already have an account? Sign in' on the welcome screen opens a sheet whose `onContinue` merely closes it (`WelcomeFooter.tsx:23,55`). A returning subscriber who reinstalls, signs in with Apple, and expects to be back in their app is dropped at the start of onboarding, still unentitled, and must find 'Restore purchases' — which is itself buried two screens deep in Settings, which they cannot reach because they are behind the hard paywall. The only restore affordance before the gate is the tertiary button on the paywall (`PaywallStandIn.tsx:31`).
proposed_fix: After a successful sign-in from welcome, identify the subscription SDK with the account, fetch the entitlement, and if entitled route straight past onboarding to the app (or to a short 'Welcome back — restoring your conditions' screen); if not entitled, route to the paywall with a message explaining that the account has no active subscription.
also_titled: "Already have an account? Sign in" on the welcome screens does nothing but close a sheet
verifier_note: The dead end is real in Phase 1: WelcomeFooter.tsx:23,55 passes `onContinue={() => setSheet(null)}`, so a successful signIn in SignInScreen.tsx:33 only closes the sheet with no entitlement refresh. But Phase 2 already schedules identity and restore (P2-T06-adapty.md:22 `identify(supabaseUid)` on every session; P2-T08-sync.md:22-23 the sign-in restore flow), and once entitlement flips the RootNavigator guards (RootNavigator.tsx:23-27) stop permitting onboarding, so the "stuck behind the hard paywall forever" outcome is not established.

title: Settings was split into a compact screen plus an undocumented "More settings" page; the Camera permission row is missing and required rows are buried behind mislabelled taps
description: The Settings tab now shows a short screen (Account, five permission rows, Units, "More preferences", "Manage subscription", "Help & feedback", "Privacy & terms", "More settings") that hides everything else behind a second page. Concretely: the Camera permission row required by the spec is absent from the top-level list - `permissionOrder` omits `'camera'` even though `settingsCopy.permissionNames` defines it and the detailed screen renders all six; tapping "Manage subscription" does not manage a subscription, it opens the More-settings page; tapping "Privacy & terms" does not open the legal document screens that exist at /settings/legal/[doc], it also opens More settings. Subscription plan/renewal, Restore purchases, Locked apps, Saved gyms, Share, Rate, Account deletion and the 7-tap version footer all live only on the second page. Because "more" is component state rather than a route, the OS back gesture does not return and the page persists across tab switches. The spec defines a single Settings screen with a fixed required row set; nothing describes a two-tier split. The compact screen's row titles are also English literals outside src/content, against the repo's content convention.
proposed_fix: Add `'camera'` to permissionOrder; point "Manage subscription" and "Privacy & terms" at their real destinations; make More settings a route (/settings/more) so back works; move the literals into src/content/settings.ts. If the two-tier layout is intentional, record it in 02-screen-inventory.md.
questions_for_johan: Settings is now a short screen plus a hidden "More settings" page, which is not what 02-screen-inventory.md:161-171 describes. Is the two-tier split the intended design (and should the inventory be updated), or should Settings go back to one screen with the required rows visible?
Is the two-level Settings (compact list + 'More settings') the intended shape? If so the screen inventory needs rewriting; if not, the subscription and legal rows should return to the top level.
also_titled: Required Settings rows are buried behind an unlabelled 'More settings' screen; 'Manage subscription' leads nowhere
'Manage subscription' never opens the App Store subscription page
verifier_note: The mechanics check out: `permissionOrder` omits 'camera' (app-next/src/features/settings/SettingsScreen.tsx:12) while DetailedSettingsScreen renders all six from `c.permissionNames` (DetailedSettingsScreen.tsx:106-118), and both `c.manage` and "Privacy & terms" call `setMore(true)` (SettingsScreen.tsx:68,71) instead of the real subscription and /settings/legal/[doc] destinations that exist (app-next/app/settings/legal/[doc].tsx); the split is undocumented against plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:161-171 and the compact rows are English literals. Two sub-claims are wrong: Account (and therefore account deletion) is reachable from the compact screen (SettingsScreen.tsx:26-30), and DetailedSettingsScreen has a "‹ Settings" back row (DetailedSettingsScreen.tsx:85), so the user is not stranded. Real but narrower than "required rows buried": medium.

title: No grace-period / billing-retry entitlement status, though Phase 2 requires mapping one
description: `Entitlement.status` is `'unknown'|'none'|'trial'|'active'|'expired'|'billingIssue'` (`src/domain/types.ts:71-73`). `plans/rebuild/phase-2-backend/P2-T06-adapty.md:26` requires mapping Adapty's grace period. Apple's billing grace period keeps the subscription *entitled* while payment retries; with only `billingIssue`, which is treated as not entitled at `RootNavigator.tsx:13`, a user in grace loses the entire app during the window Apple explicitly grants them. There is no copy anywhere for 'we're retrying your payment, you still have access'.
proposed_fix: Add a `grace` status that counts as entitled, show a persistent non-blocking 'Update payment method' banner, and map Adapty's grace-period flag to it in P2-T06.
verifier_note: Real gap in the domain contract: `Entitlement.status` has no grace value (app-next/src/domain/types.ts:71-73), `entitled` is trial||active (RootNavigator.tsx:13), and no copy exists for a payment retry, while P2-T06:26 requires mapping Adapty's grace period. Severity is lower than stated because the adapter can map Adapty's still-active grace profile onto `active` and keep access; what is genuinely missing is a distinct state and the "update payment method" messaging.

title: Session carries no user id, so the Adapty↔Supabase identity spine cannot exist
description: `Session` is `{kind:'anonymous'} | {kind:'signedIn'; provider; email}` (`src/domain/types.ts:74-76`) — no user id. Decision D3 (`plans/rebuild/00-decisions.md:62`) requires the Adapty customer id to be the Supabase uid, and `P2-T10-settings-account-wiring.md:5-8` builds on that identity. Additionally, grep of `src` and `app` finds zero call sites for `subscription.identify`, `subscription.reset`, `analytics.identify`, `analytics.reset`, `auth.session` and `auth.subscribe`; the app reads `sessionStore`/`entitlementStore` directly. As shipped, signing in never tells the subscription or analytics SDK who the user is, so purchases made anonymously and purchases made signed-in cannot be reconciled, and a second device will not see the entitlement.
proposed_fix: Add `userId` to the signed-in session; on sign-in call `subscription.identify(userId)` and `analytics.identify(userId)`, on sign-out call the matching `reset()`. Add a test asserting the ordering.
verifier_note: Confirmed that `Session` carries no user id (app-next/src/domain/types.ts:74-76, AuthPort.ts:3-11) and that `identify`/`reset` have no production call sites (only fakes at demo/fakes/AnalyticsFake.ts:7 and SubscriptionFake.ts:29-30). Overstated, though: P2-T06:3 already schedules `identify(supabaseUid)` on every session including anonymous, with the Supabase uid as Adapty's `customer_user_id` per D3, and the adapter can read that uid from the Supabase client without the domain `Session` carrying it.

title: Two conditions met the same day: the card can flip between them as progress ticks
area: Home / unlock hint / Domain / stacking / unlockedMet attribution
description: When two conditions are met on the same day, `byRuleId` is decided by the position of the met rows in the RuleDay array (the sort is by day only, and is stable). Verified: rows [A,B] → A; rows [B,A] → B. `progressSync` patches days as `[...unchanged, ...changes]`, so any row that changes moves to the end — meaning a second condition still accruing progress can overtake the first and change which rule is reported as the unlocker. Once the UI shows the unlocking condition (see the missing-attribution finding) this becomes a visible flip.
evidence: app-next/src/domain/resolveLock.ts:29-31 — the first surviving row wins and sets byRuleId
app-next/src/domain/types.ts:97 — unlockedMet carries a single byRuleId
proposed_fix: Break the tie deterministically on `metAt` (earliest met wins) rather than array position, and cover it with a test.
questions_for_johan: When two locked conditions are in different units — 100 steps left vs 20 minutes of running — which one should Home tell the user to do? The model says 'smallest remaining effort, with immediate actions ranked first', which contradicts itself for this case.
When two conditions are met the same day, should the card credit the one met first, or the one that would otherwise be hardest?
also_titled: Which condition Home advertises depends on invisible array order, and editing an unrelated condition changes it
When two rules are met on the same day the Home card names an arbitrary one
verifier_note: app-next/src/domain/resolveLock.ts:23 sorts by day only, so with two met rows for the same day the first array element wins, and app-next/src/features/home/progressSync.ts:52-57 rebuilds days as [...unchanged, ...changes], moving any still-accruing row to the end. It is user-visible today: app-next/src/features/home/HomeScreen.tsx:80-88 feeds byRuleId into blockingSchedule, whose card prints that rule's window, icon and condition line (app-next/src/features/home/blockingSchedule.ts:5-22).

title: Editing a walking condition into a step goal skips the goal screen and silently applies the 5,000 default
description: Edit opens at the mode step (S3). Choosing a different mode calls `createDraft`, which resets the draft to defaults (5,000 steps, 30 gym minutes, 20/30 running/biking minutes), and `next()` in edit mode jumps straight back to S3 — the goal step is never shown. So changing 'Unlock while walking' to a step goal saves a 5,000-step goal the user never chose, and changing 'Arrive at the gym' to 'Spend time at the gym' saves 30 minutes and skips the place step.
proposed_fix: In edit mode, when the mode changes, continue through the goal step (and the gym place step for gym-time) before returning to the summary; preserve the existing goal when the mode is unchanged.
verifier_note: The outcome is real: edit opens at the S3 summary (app-next/src/features/conditions/useBuilder.ts:34), the Activity row's edit target is goalStep (app-next/src/features/rules/PlanSummary.tsx:23), which is the mode chooser W2/G1 for state and arrival rules (app-next/src/features/rules/plan.ts:34-35), and next() with a backup jumps straight to S3 (useBuilder.ts:80-82), so the goal step and GPlace are never shown and the untouched defaults (5,000 steps / 30 min from draft.ts:38-39, set by fromRule's createDraft at draft.ts:97) are saved. The cited mechanism is wrong though: createDraft is only called by choose() on O20 (useBuilder.ts:56-59), which edit mode never reaches.

title: Half of the mode changes are impossible, and activity can never be changed at all
description: `goalStep` sends the edit flow to a fixed step per mode, so a step-goal walking condition can never become 'unlock while walking', a gym-minutes condition can never become gym-arrival, and a distance condition can never become minutes — the chooser is simply not on the path. Activity (walking / gym / running / biking) is never editable at all. The user's only route is delete + recreate, which (per the delete finding) re-locks their apps and loses today's progress.
proposed_fix: Make the edit entry a summary screen with 'Activity', 'Goal', 'Days', 'Time' rows, each opening its own step, instead of a linear replay of creation.
verifier_note: app-next/src/features/rules/plan.ts:33-37 sends the summary's only activity edit to a fixed goal step, so a target walking rule lands on W3 and can never reach the W2 mode chooser, gym-minutes lands on G2 and never G1, and distance lands on D and never R1/B1; PlanSummary's other rows are only W1 (walking place) and S1 (app-next/src/features/rules/PlanSummary.tsx:22-28). O20 is unreachable in edit mode (useBuilder.ts:34 starts at S3 and back() with a backup returns to S3), so activity is never editable, and delete+recreate loses the day's RuleDay rows (mutations.ts:16-23).

title: The gym picker is unreachable from a gym rule, and gym rules carry no gym reference at all
area: Conditions / gym + multiple gyms / Gyms / gym · presence
description: A user with two saved gyms cannot tell a condition which one it means, and cannot get to the gym picker from the condition. `RuleMode` for gym-event and gym-minutes carries no place id, so a gym rule applies to whichever saved gym the user happens to be nearest; editing a gym rule offers no gym row on the summary and `GPlace` is not an edit target. The screen inventory lists the gym rule's progress card as one of the three entry points to SH-gym, but that card's action now routes to /unlock/gym, so from a gym rule there is no path to the picker at all - only Settings > Saved gyms. Deleting a saved gym also gives no warning that gym conditions may be left with nothing to detect.
evidence: app-next/src/features/unlock/useGymUnlock.ts:21-25 (nearest = sort saved places by distance from the last sample)
app-next/src/runtime/ForegroundGym.ts:15-24 (presence is any place within radius; the id is discarded)
docs/specs/aha-unlock-screens.md:186-188 ("with overlapping radii the nearest gym wins")
proposed_fix: Either add an optional `placeId` to the gym rule modes with a "Gym" row on the plan summary, or state explicitly in 01-product-model.md that a gym rule matches any saved gym and remove the gym-rule entry point from the SH-gym row. Also warn on deleting a gym while gym conditions exist.
questions_for_johan: Should a gym condition point at one specific saved gym, or should any of the five saved gyms satisfy every gym condition? The code does the latter with no way to change it, and the screen inventory implies the former.
also_titled: Gym conditions carry no place, so any gym credits every gym condition
GymPort's presence signal carries no place id, so the app guesses which gym you are at

PlanSummary offers no gym row and GPlace is never an edit target (app-next/src/features/rules/plan.ts:33-37, PlanSummary.tsx:22-28), while HomeScreen.tsx:101-105 routes a gym card to /unlock/gym, so the SH-gym entry point promised at plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:180 ("gym rule progress card") does not exist except via the noGym fallback at GymUnlockScreen.tsx:68-69.

title: Deleting a saved gym gives no consequence copy and silently orphans gym conditions
area: Settings / gyms / settings/gyms / gym · saved places
description: User experience: the user removes their only saved gym. The confirmation sheet is titled "Remove gym", its body is just the gym's name, its confirm button also says "Remove gym" and its cancel says "Close". Nothing warns that their "Arrive at the gym" condition will now never fire. After deleting, the Conditions screen still shows "Arrive at the gym" with its switch on and its schedule, and Home still shows the "I'm at the gym" entry pill; only opening the unlock ceremony reveals "Save a gym first". app-next/src/features/home/progressContent.ts:31-39 (card copy is unaffected by having zero gyms)

title: At the 5-gym cap, adding a gym condition silently overwrites an existing gym
description: The builder's gym step renders the picker with `placeId={gyms[gyms.length - 1]?.id}`, i.e. it edits the most recently saved gym rather than creating a new one. A user at the 5-gym cap (Settings correctly disables 'Add gym' at 5) who creates a sixth gym condition will silently rewrite gym #5 — breaking any other condition that pointed at it. There is no message about the cap anywhere in the builder.
proposed_fix: In the builder, pick from existing gyms or add a new one; when the cap is reached, say so and require a pick.
verifier_note: app-next/src/features/gym-picker/BuilderGymStep.tsx:5 passes placeId={gyms[gyms.length-1]?.id}, which usePicker turns into `existing` and saves under that id (app-next/src/features/gym-picker/usePicker.ts:9,167), so the builder's gym step overwrites the most recent saved gym instead of adding one, and usePicker.ts:141-142 suppresses the cap warning because the existing id is already in the list. If anything the finding understates it: the overwrite happens at any gym count of one or more, not only at the five-gym cap enforced in GymsScreen.tsx:74.

title: Gym-minutes progress only accrues from live presence, so a gym visit before the condition existed counts as zero
description: Steps and workout minutes are day totals, so creating a condition at noon correctly counts the morning's activity. Gym dwell time is accumulated tick-by-tick from a live arrival only, so a user who was at the gym at 08:00 and creates (or unpauses) a 'spend 30 minutes at the gym' condition at 12:00 sees 0 / 30 min and stays locked all day. Decision B8 measures progress from the start of the local day, and the model calls gym target progress 'geofence dwell time today'.
proposed_fix: Keep dwell time as a per-day accumulator independent of which rules exist, and evaluate rules against that day total.
verifier_note: app-next/src/demo/gymProgress.ts:23-45 credits only the minutes elapsed since the last tick while presence is 'inside', into a row that defaults to progress 0 for a rule that did not exist earlier, and nothing backfills from the day history in app-next/src/demo/activityHistory.ts:20-33 (which itself derives gym minutes from those same rows). That contradicts plans/rebuild/00-decisions.md:33 (B8, progress from the start of the local day) and plans/rebuild/01-product-model.md:159 ('geofence dwell time today'). A user who left the gym before creating the rule sees 0 of 30 min.

title: Creating a condition whose window has already started locks the apps the moment the user taps Save
description: There is no acknowledgement anywhere in the builder that the window the user just chose is already running. A user setting 9 AM–9 PM at 3 PM taps 'Save condition' and lands on Home with every chosen app blocked and a goal they have not started. The summary step shows the schedule but no 'This starts now' note, and there is no post-save confirmation.
proposed_fix: On the summary step, when the window covers 'now', say 'Blocking starts as soon as you save' and show what still has to be done today to unlock.
verifier_note: app-next/src/features/conditions/useBuilder.ts:84-87 saves and closes with no check of whether the chosen window covers 'now', and the summary step's only copy is app-next/src/content/plan.ts:10-11,20-21 ('Your plan is ready', 'Unlocks your apps for the rest of the day') — nothing says blocking begins immediately. Because resolveLock locks inside an active window until met (app-next/src/domain/resolveLock.ts:36-41), a 9 AM–9 PM rule saved at 3 PM locks on the spot with no acknowledgement anywhere in the flow.

title: The gym check-in AbortController is wired only to unmount, not to leaving the gym
description: If the user walks out of the geofence mid-ring, the hook resets its own visual state but never aborts the in-flight check-in request. Correctness depends entirely on the fake choosing to reject with 'Left gym'. A real adapter that resolves optimistically, or that misses the presence change, would credit an arrival the user abandoned.
evidence: app-next/src/features/unlock/useGymUnlock.ts:59 — abort() called from the unmount cleanup only
app-next/src/features/unlock/useGymUnlock.ts:44-54 — the presence === 'outside' branch resets state but does not abort

title: Progress rows are written for days the rule is not scheduled, and the two writers disagree about which day owns them

title: WalkingFake.resume double-counts minutes after a relaunch
description: Relaunching mid-walk can credit more minutes than were walked: resume computes its baseline from the scenario's own walking script while playback uses the default script, so when a scenario carries no walking script the two disagree and the elapsed time is counted twice.
evidence: app-next/src/demo/walkingProgress.ts:4-8 — the write that receives the doubled value
proposed_fix: Resolve the script once (scenario script or default) and use the same resolved script in both resume() and play(); write progress as an absolute 'minutes since startedAt' value rather than an increment, so replay is idempotent.
verifier_note: app-next/src/demo/fakes/WalkingFake.ts:68-70 derives its baseline only from ctx.scenario.walking (seconds = 0 when absent), while play() at line 21-24 falls back to the default script and re-adds walkedSeconds, so resume passes base = existing progress and then writes base + seconds again (line 36). writeWalkingProgress overwrites with that absolute value (app-next/src/demo/walkingProgress.ts:7), so the elapsed minutes are counted twice after a relaunch.

title: Shield copy bakes a live number into Apple's static template, which only refreshes when the app runs

Because steps only update in the foreground, a user who walks 1,700 of their 1,800 remaining steps then taps Instagram sees a shield still claiming 1,800 to go. The research doc states the rule explicitly: "Copy must be designed for staleness, not live numbers."
proposed_fix: Replace `shieldProgress` with a staleness-safe form that names the goal rather than the remainder ("Walk 5,000 steps to open your apps" / "Open ExcerLock to check your steps"), and keep the live remainder for Home only. title: applyLock is fire-and-forget with no failure channel, so the old app's fail-closed law is unrepresentable
description: `applyLock(decision): void` — synchronous, no promise, no error, no acknowledgement. A caller can never learn that the shield was not applied or that a DeviceActivity monitor failed to register. The old app's rule was explicit: if registering the renewal monitor fails, apply the shield before returning the error, i.e. fail closed. With a `void` return there is no error to return and no way for Home or the diagnostics log to say "blocking is not actually on". The port also carries no idempotency contract, so a caller ticking once a second would call it 86,400 times a day (P2-T04 promises idempotency in the adapter, but the interface does not).
proposed_fix: Change the signature to `applyLock(decision): Promise<{ applied: boolean; reason?: string }>` (or add an `observeEnforcement` channel), document the fail-closed law in `src/ports/README.md`, and surface a failure as a Home state and a diagnostics entry. Update the architecture port table at 04-architecture.md:65 to match.
verifier_note: app-next/src/ports/ScreenTimePort.ts:7 declares `applyLock(decision: LockDecision): void` and plans/rebuild/04-architecture.md:65 repeats that signature, so no caller can learn the shield was not applied. The old app's enforcement path fails closed explicitly — app/src/screentime/native/NativeShieldScheduler.ts:196-199 and 232-242 call blockSelection before rethrowing — and P2-T04:9-11 only promises adapter idempotency, with no failure channel, Home state or diagnostics entry anywhere in the plan.

title: An unmet second condition's window never re-locks after another condition is met, and nothing says so
description: User experience: the user has "Walk 5,000 steps, Mon–Fri 9–12" and "Run 20 minutes, daily 18–22". They hit the step goal at 10:00. At 18:00 the second condition's blocking window opens — and nothing locks. Home says "Unlocked for the rest of today / Blocking resumes tomorrow at 9 AM", the Conditions screen shows both conditions with their switches on and their schedules, and nothing explains that the evening one is inert today. What the code says: `relockAt` is `nextInstanceStart(enabled, cutoff - 1ms)` where `cutoff` is the local midnight *after* the met day, so no window on the same day can ever re-lock; `statusContent` only reports the relock time.
proposed_fix: When `unlockedMet` is active, mark the other scheduled conditions as satisfied wherever they appear: add a "Met by <condition> today" support line to the Home condition rows, and a "Satisfied today" badge on `RuleCard`. This makes B6 legible rather than looking like a bug.

title: Offline is unhandled everywhere except the gym search
description: User experience: with no network, a purchase, a restore, a sign-in, an email code and a support send all collapse into the same generic "Something went wrong.
