verifier_note: haptics.ts:4-7 exports `setHapticsEnabled` and grep over app-next/src and app-next/app finds no caller; PreferencesPanel.tsx:66-71 only writes settingsStore.haptics (settingsStore.ts:10,14) and nothing reads it back, so the module-level `enabled` at haptics.ts:4 stays true forever. PreferencesPanel.tsx:69 also fires `feedback()` before the write, so the confirming tap buzzes even as the user turns it off.

title: Gym auto-detect switch silently swallows a denied Always-location grant
description: `PreferencesPanel.tsx:51-55` does `if (v) void runtime.gym.enableAutoDetect(); else runtime.gym.disableAutoDetect();` — the boolean returned by `enableAutoDetect` (`src/demo/fakes/GymFake.ts:95-107`, which requires an Always grant) is discarded. A user who flips the switch on and then denies (or has previously denied) Always location sees the switch snap back with no explanation of why, and no route to the location permission detail. Auto-detect is the feature that makes gym conditions work unattended, so a silent failure here silently breaks gym rules.
proposed_fix: Await the result; on false show an inline explanation ('Auto-detect needs Always location') with a button that requests or opens Settings, and keep the switch off.
verifier_note: PreferencesPanel.tsx:51-55 discards the boolean from `enableAutoDetect`, which GymFake.ts:95-107 returns false from whenever the Always-location prompt is not granted (it only patches the store on success). The switch is bound to `s.gymAutoDetect` (:49) so it snaps back with no message and no route to PermissionDetail.tsx:26's Open Settings action.

title: Trial timeline and reminder copy are hardcoded rather than derived from the offer
description: `src/content/subscription.ts:2` defines the offer (`trialDays: 7`, `reminderDaysBefore: 2`), but line 12 hardcodes '2 days before your trial ends' and lines 19-23 hardcode 'Day 5 · Reminder' and 'Day 7 · Billing begins'. `TrialScreen.tsx:13` reads the real offer from `runtime.subscription.entitlement().offer`. When Phase 2 supplies Adapty's actual trial length (or an experiment changes it), the screen will show a correct trial length in one place and a wrong Day 5/Day 7 timeline in another, and promise a reminder on the wrong date.
proposed_fix: Make the timeline and reminder strings functions of `offer.trialDays` and `offer.reminderDaysBefore`, and take those from the live Adapty offer in Phase 2.
verifier_note: subscription.ts:2 defines trialDays 7 / reminderDaysBefore 2, but :12 hardcodes '2 days before your trial ends' and :19-23 hardcode 'Day 5 · Reminder' and 'Day 7 · Billing begins', while TrialScreen.tsx:13,35 reads the live offer only for `offer.label`. P2-T06-adapty.md:18-24 wires the real Adapty offer and decision E4 (00-decisions.md) says the 7-day trial is a design example, so the timeline will state a wrong billing day with no plan item to derive it.

title: Support form has no reply path or confirmation of where the message goes
description: Settings routes to `support` from both levels (`SettingsScreen.tsx:70`, `DetailedSettingsScreen.tsx:165`), but the support screen collects a message with no stated destination, no email address captured for anonymous users (who are the majority under B18), and `SupportPort`'s fake only logs. A user whose lock is stuck sends a message and never hears back, and we have no address to reply to.
proposed_fix: Require a reply-to email when the session is anonymous, attach diagnostic context (entitlement status, permission states, app version), and confirm on send where the message went and the expected response time.
verifier_note: SupportScreen.tsx:44-47 collects only a category chip and a message; SupportPort.ts:2 is `send(category, message)` with no contact address or context field, and no settings screen collects an email (grep for "email" in app-next/src/features/settings/*.tsx returns nothing), so an anonymous user under B18 (plans/rebuild/00-decisions.md:39) leaves no reply channel, and the sent copy at app-next/src/content/settings.ts:94-95 states neither destination nor response time. It is more than a copy gap: excerlock-app-prd.md:297 requires the composer to auto-attach app version, iOS version, device, entitlement state and permission statuses "user-visible before send", which neither the screen nor the port contract can express, and section F (plans/rebuild/00-decisions.md:78-85) does not cut it. Severity raised to medium because a Phase-1 port signature has to change for the spec'd behaviour to be possible.

title: An abandoned treadmill scan becomes a verified unlock after relaunch
description: A user starts a propped scan, never completes it, force-quits, and reopens the app — the session is now 'walking' and the apps are unlocked, with no camera verification ever having happened. start() with placement 'propped' leaves the session in 'verifying' without playback, but resume() replays the default script from startedAt on relaunch, which promotes the phase to 'walking', and resolveLock treats a walking session as an unlock.
evidence: app-next/src/demo/fakes/WalkingFake.ts:60 — propped start leaves phase 'verifying' with no playback
app-next/src/demo/fakes/WalkingFake.ts:63-74 — resume() recomputes phase from elapsed using the script, promoting 'verifying' to 'walking'
app-next/src/domain/resolveLock.ts:16-22 — a session with phase 'walking' yields state 'unlockedWalking'
docs/specs/treadmill-mode.md:73-118 — verification is required before the walk counts
proposed_fix: Persist the verification outcome alongside the session and have resume() refuse to advance a propped session past 'verifying' unless a completed scan was recorded; an unverified propped session older than the scan timeout should resume as 'ended'.
verifier_note: resume() (WalkingFake.ts:63-74) does replay an abandoned propped session through play(), whose phase comes from elapsed (WalkingFake.ts:26-29). With the default/only script (['verifying','walking','grace','ended'], stepMs 6000, scenarios/home-walking-session.ts:6) elapsed ≥ 24 s resolves to 'ended', so the phantom 'walking'/'grace' unlock only occurs when the user relaunches within roughly 6–24 s of starting the scan and lasts seconds.

title: The lock card timeline describes only one condition's window, so stacked windows are drawn wrong
description: A user with 'Mon–Fri 9:00–12:00' and 'daily 18:00–22:00' sees a single card reading 'Block from 9 AM to 12 PM' with a timeline of that one window. The 18:00–22:00 block is invisible on Home; at 19:00 the apps are locked while the card says blocking runs 9–12. `blockingSchedule` takes exactly one rule (the earliest-starting scheduled rule) and renders its window as if it were the whole day's blocking picture. The decision register explicitly permits overlapping and disjoint windows.
proposed_fix: Compute the union of today's window instances and render every segment on the timeline, with the summary line reading e.g. '9 AM–12 PM and 6 PM–10 PM'. Add a scenario with two disjoint windows.
verifier_note: The stated failure does not occur: resolveLock.ts:39 builds `nextUnlockHint` from `active` rules only, so at 19:00 the hint rule is B and HomeScreen.tsx:76-77 feeds B's 6 PM–10 PM window to the card, not 9–12. The card is also not "the earliest-starting scheduled rule" except in `beforeWindow` (resolveLock.ts:41-45). The residual truth is only that blockingSchedule.ts:5-23 renders one window at a time, so the day's other window is not previewed — a completeness gap, not a wrong lock picture.

title: Paywall offers a Lifetime plan that the PRD explicitly ruled out
description: The paywall lists three plans including `{ id:'lifetime', title:'Lifetime', price:'$–.–– once' }` at `src/content/subscription.ts:29`. `excerlock-app-prd.md:383` decides 'no weekly, no lifetime'. Whichever is stale, a reviewer or a user sees a purchase option the product decided not to sell, and a lifetime SKU also breaks the trial-reminder and renewal copy (`c.renewal`, 'Day 7 · Billing begins').
proposed_fix: Remove the lifetime row from the Phase 1 fixture, or, if lifetime is back on, update the PRD line and define how lifetime interacts with the trial timeline, renewal row and the trial reminder.
questions_for_johan: Is there going to be a Lifetime product in App Store Connect / Adapty? The Phase 1 paywall offers one; no spec or catalog does.
Is Lifetime a real SKU for v1? The PRD line 383 says 'no weekly, no lifetime' but the paywall fixture offers it.
also_titled: The paywall offers a "Lifetime" plan that no source promises and no product catalog contains
verifier_note: The conflict is real — `{ id:'lifetime', ... }` at app-next/src/content/subscription.ts:28 against "no weekly, no lifetime" at excerlock-app-prd.md:383. But this is an explicitly labelled Phase 1 stand-in with `$–.––` placeholder prices (subscription.ts:1, plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:95), and decision E4 (plans/rebuild/00-decisions.md:74) hands real prices/plans to the Adapty dashboard, so no user can ever buy a lifetime SKU from this build. Copy hygiene, not a shipping risk: low.

title: HealthPort cannot express the one anti-cheat the PRD keeps: manually entered workouts must not count
description: A user types a fake 30-minute run into Apple Health and unlocks their apps. `HealthPort.workoutsToday` returns `{kind, minutes, km}` — no source flag, no `wasUserEntered`, no start time, no sample id. So the device-recorded-only filter cannot be stated at the port boundary, cannot be exercised by a fake or a scenario, and cannot be asserted by the port-level contract tests Phase 2 promises to reuse. The same missing id means two overlapping samples (iPhone + Watch, or an app that writes a duplicate) are summed twice, and the missing start time means "workouts started today" is unverifiable from the port's own data. This is the only HealthKit anti-cheat the PRD leaves in place, and the old app implemented it (`getTodayTotal` drops `wasUserEntered`; `appleExerciseTime` and workout durations are never summed).
evidence: excerlock-app-prd.md:102 ("one filter, no fraud-detection system — earning means you actually did it")
proposed_fix: Widen `Workout` to `{ id: string; kind; startedAt: string; minutes: number; km: number; manuallyEntered: boolean }`, have `progressSync` drop `manuallyEntered` samples and de-duplicate on `id`, and add a `manual-entry-day` scenario mirroring the old app's adversarial fixture so the rule is proven in Phase 1 and re-proven by the Phase 2 adapter.
verifier_note: `Workout = { kind; minutes; km }` (app-next/src/ports/models.ts:28) does lack a source flag, id and start time, so the fake cannot produce a manual sample. But the anti-cheat itself is already scheduled inside the adapter — P2-T05:46-48 says `workoutsToday` returns "device-recorded workouts started today (manual entries excluded as before)" with fixture-driven contract tests at :49-50 — and filtering/de-duplicating before returning needs no port-shape change, so this is a testability preference rather than a user-facing hole.

title: Nothing implements the propped→handheld→handoff state machine; a propped session just dies at 15 minutes
description: A user on a treadmill picks their phone up mid-walk to change a song, or sets it back down, or simply keeps walking past the 15-minute lease. In all three cases nothing happens except that the lease eventually expires and the session is set to `ended` — the apps re-lock and the user must re-open the app and re-scan with no prompt telling them so. The spec's SCANNING/PROPPED/HANDHELD/HANDOFF machine — 20 s pickup cadence grace, 60 s put-down handoff, put-down pausing the exit grace, a successful motion verification resetting the propped lease, lease expiry returning to SCANNING rather than ending the session — has no representation in `app-next`: the shipped controller phases are scan-only (`idle | scanning | needsFraming | verified | permissionDenied | expired`) and `WalkingPort` has no placement-change signal beyond a poll-only `treadmillFraming()`.
evidence: app-next/src/ports/WalkingPort.ts:4-9 (start/stop/completeProppedScan/observe/details/treadmillFraming — no placement events, no lease renewal)
app-next/src/demo/fakes/WalkingFake.ts:86 (lease expiry simply calls stop() → phase 'ended')
docs/specs/treadmill-mode.md:73-104 (PROPPED / HANDHELD / HANDOFF, the 20 s and 60 s graces, put-down pauses exit grace, lease restarts on scan)
proposed_fix: Model the four phases in `WalkingSession` (or a sibling `placement` field) so the domain and the UI can see them, add a placement-change subscription to `WalkingPort`, and give the treadmill screen a `needsRescan` state fed by lease expiry. This is P2-T05's `WalkingAdapter` work, but the port and the session type have to widen first or the ported controller has nowhere to publish.
verifier_note: Correct that Phase 1 has no PROPPED/HANDHELD/HANDOFF machine (TreadmillScanController.ts:6 is scan-only, WalkingPort.ts:4-9 has no placement events, WalkingFake.ts:86 ends the session on lease expiry), but the plan already owns it: P2-T05:13-17 ports `walkingSessionController` and the `scanning → propped → handheld → handoff` flow and explicitly decides phases stay mapped 1:1 to the Phase 1 script, and P2-T04:15-17 covers lease expiry re-shielding plus the 30 s warning. The finding's specific claim that the port and `WalkingSession` must widen first is contradicted by that plan text.

title: A step-goal rule can be created with place 'Treadmill' even though a propped phone counts no steps
description: A user picks "Treadmill" at W1 and then "Reach a step goal" at W2 — the recommended option — and gets a rule that is unreachable in the way they said they exercise: the pedometer reads ~zero for a phone propped on a console, which is the exact problem the treadmill spec was written to solve. There is no treadmill entry, no ceremony and no camera path for target rules (`unlockKind` returns null unless the mode is `state`), and nothing anywhere warns them. Onboarding asks the place question before the mode question, so the combination is the natural path for a treadmill user who takes the recommended mode.
evidence: app-next/src/features/conditions/builderFlow.ts (W1 place → W2 mode → W3 goal; place is asked first)
app-next/src/features/home/progressSync.ts:37-38 (walking target progress is the raw pedometer total)
docs/specs/treadmill-mode.md:11-16 (a propped phone reports zero steps — the whole reason the mode exists)
docs/specs/aha-unlock-screens.md:25-26 (step-target walking is explicitly excluded from the ceremony)
proposed_fix: Either drop the `place` field for target-mode walking rules (ask W1 only after the user chooses "Unlock while walking"), or, if the place stays, show a warning on W2/S3 for treadmill + step goal and steer the user to "Unlock while walking".
questions_for_johan: When someone says they walk on a treadmill, should the step-goal option be hidden or discouraged (since a propped phone counts no steps), or should the treadmill place simply not be asked until they pick "Unlock while walking"?
verifier_note: The combination is creatable — W1 place precedes W2 mode (builderFlow.ts:6-7, content/rules.ts:2-3), target walking carries a `place` (domain/types.ts:15), `unlockKind` gives target rules no treadmill path (entry.ts:2-5), and grep of app-next/src finds no warning for treadmill + step goal. But the premise is overstated: docs/specs/treadmill-mode.md:11-16 says treadmill walking counts normally whenever the phone travels with the body, so the rule is unreachable only for a propped phone, making this a missing warning rather than a broken rule.

title: The paywall plan picker is cosmetic — every plan grants the same trial
description: The user chooses Annual, Monthly or Lifetime and taps the CTA; `SubscriptionFake.presentPaywall` (`src/demo/fakes/SubscriptionFake.ts:9-18`) ignores the selection entirely and always grants `{status:'trial'}`. The selected plan id is never passed to the port — `SubscriptionPort.presentPaywall` takes only a placement. Even the CTA label changes on selection (`PaywallStandIn.tsx:26`) while the outcome does not. In Phase 1 this hides the fact that no purchase path is plan-aware; in Phase 2 Adapty's Paywall Builder owns the selection, so the whole local picker may be dead UI.
proposed_fix: Either pass the selected package through the port and have the fake produce a plan-specific entitlement (so purchase state is testable), or drop the local picker and state in the screen inventory that Adapty's hosted paywall renders the plans.
verifier_note: Accurate mechanically: `PaywallSlot` keeps `selected` in local state and never passes it to `presentPaywall(placement)` (app-next/src/features/subscription/PaywallSlot.tsx:12,33-35; SubscriptionPort.ts:7), and the fake always grants a trial (SubscriptionFake.ts:9-18). But decision C6 (plans/rebuild/00-decisions.md:52) and 02-screen-inventory.md:95 declare the Phase 1 screen a stand-in whose only job is to make the flow testable, with the Adapty Builder owning plan selection in Phase 2 (P2-T06:2), so this is expected placeholder behaviour.

title: A paused condition looks identical to an active one on the Conditions screen
description: User experience: the user pauses a condition. The card looks exactly the same — same icon tint, same title, same schedule line, same card background — with only a small switch flipped. Turning off every condition changes nothing at all on the Conditions screen; the only place the app says anything is Home ("All conditions are paused"). A user scanning the list cannot see which conditions are actually in force today, whether one is scheduled today at all, or whether one has already been met. What the code says: `RuleCard` applies no dimming, no badge and no tone change based on `enabled`, and `ConditionsScreen` passes no day/met/scheduled information at all.
proposed_fix: Add a status line to `RuleCard` driven by the same data Home already has: "Paused", "Not scheduled today", "Active now · 1,240 / 5,000 steps", "Met today". Dim the card (reduced opacity on icon and title) while paused so the list is scannable at a glance.
also_titled: Paused conditions look exactly like active ones, and a partly-paused set has no signal anywhere
Pausing every condition changes nothing on the Conditions screen
verifier_note: The code claims hold — RuleCard applies no enabled-driven tone (app-next/src/design-system/RuleCard.tsx:58-115) and ConditionsScreen passes no day/met data (ConditionsScreen.tsx:49-61) — but plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:137-138 specifies the card as exactly icon, title, schedule and switch, so nothing planned is missing. The switch itself is the standard iOS paused affordance and the schedule line already says which days a condition runs, so this is a polish suggestion rather than a gap.

title: The Conditions screen shows no per-condition state — no met, no progress, no 'blocking now'
description: The list renders name, schedule and a switch. With four conditions the user cannot answer 'which of these is done today?', 'which one is blocking me right now?' or 'which one unlocked my apps?' from this screen at all — they have to go back to Home, which also does not say. This is the screen the user opens precisely to manage a stack.
proposed_fix: Add a per-row state chip: Met today / In progress 3,120 of 5,000 / Blocking now / Not scheduled today / Paused.
verifier_note: The list row really is name + schedule + switch only (app-next/src/features/conditions/ConditionsScreen.tsx:49-61), but that is exactly what plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:136 specifies, and the claim that Home 'also does not say' is wrong: HomeScreen renders a ProgressCard per enabled rule scheduled today with progress and detail (app-next/src/features/home/HomeScreen.tsx:89-107, app-next/src/state/selectors.ts:31-54). Real as an enhancement, not as a gap against the spec.

title: The 30-second gym cooldown runs on real wall time while the rest of the app runs on the fake clock
description: A tester who advances time in the dev menu during the gym ring sees the ring and the app disagree: the ring's progress and the fake's confirmation timeout both use real wall time, whereas sessions, leases, windows and progress use the FakeClock. Jumping the clock forward finishes a walking lease but leaves the ring where it was, and vice versa.
evidence: app-next/src/features/unlock/useGymUnlock.ts:62-80 — Date.now() plus setInterval(..., 50) drives the ring
app-next/src/demo/fakes/GymFake.ts:59-66 — setTimeout(confirmation.milliseconds) is a real-time timer
app-next/src/demo/clock.ts:13-24 — everything else derives from FakeClock
app-next/src/state/selectors.ts:23 — timezone and now come from the ClockPort
proposed_fix: Drive all product timing off the ClockPort, including the confirmation window and the ring's progress; keep Date.now only for frame-rate animation interpolation that carries no product meaning.
verifier_note: The mechanics are as described — app-next/src/features/unlock/useGymUnlock.ts:62-80 drives the ring from Date.now on a 50 ms interval and app-next/src/demo/fakes/GymFake.ts:59-66 uses a real setTimeout, while leases and windows come from the FakeClock (app-next/src/demo/clock.ts:11-24). But in production Date.now and ClockPort are the same clock, so the only person who hits the disagreement is a tester time-travelling in the dev menu.

title: afterWindow versus noRulesToday depends on whether a window happened to spill past midnight
description: Two users in the same situation — today's blocking is over, apps are open — get different copy depending on an accident of window geometry. The afterWindow test scans only yesterday and today for a window whose end day-key equals today, so a rule whose window ended at 20:00 yesterday and has none today yields noRulesToday, while an overnight rule ending at 06:00 today yields afterWindow.
evidence: app-next/src/domain/resolveLock.ts:46-49 — [addDays(today,-1), today].flatMap(...).some(w => dayKey(w.end, tz) === today && end <= now)
app-next/src/features/home/statusContent.ts:71-78 — the two branches produce different copy
proposed_fix: Define the split on intent rather than geometry: afterWindow when the rule was scheduled today and its window has ended, noRulesToday when no rule was scheduled today at all. Both should carry the next start.
verifier_note: The scan is as cited (app-next/src/domain/resolveLock.ts:46-49), but the two examples are different user situations: a window that ended at 20:00 yesterday means no blocking happened today, so noRulesToday is right, and the finding's own proposed definition ('scheduled today and ended') would not change it. What is real is the second half: noRulesToday carries no nextLockAt and Home shows 'Nothing scheduled today' (app-next/src/features/home/statusContent.ts:78, app-next/src/content/home.ts:22), where plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:104 asks for the next scheduled start.

title: "Get ahead" is offered before windows for state rules, where getting ahead is impossible
description: Before a window whose only rule is a walking state rule, Home invites the user to 'Get ahead: unlock while walking now'. State rules are never 'met' — walking progress explicitly writes met: false — so there is nothing to get ahead on; the invitation cannot be acted on in a way that changes the upcoming lock.
evidence: app-next/src/demo/walkingProgress.ts:4-8 — writes met: false for state rules
app-next/src/domain/resolveLock.ts:24 — the unlockedMet scan skips state-mode rules
proposed_fix: Pick the get-ahead rule from the enabled target-mode rules only; if the upcoming window has no target rule, show a neutral 'Blocking starts at <time>' instead.
verifier_note: beforeWindow really does take the earliest-starting rule regardless of mode and wrap its name in 'Get ahead: … now' (app-next/src/features/home/statusContent.ts:71-78, app-next/src/content/home.ts:25), so a state rule yields 'Get ahead: unlock while walking now'. But 'cannot be acted on' is overstated: a walking session started before the window is still live when the window opens and resolveLock then returns unlockedWalking (app-next/src/domain/resolveLock.ts:16-22), so this is awkward copy rather than a broken invitation.

title: localInstant gives up after three iterations and returns its last guess unchecked
description: For an exotic zone with a sub-hour or historically shifting offset, the fixed-point loop can exit without converging and the function returns a guess that does not correspond to the requested local time — producing a window that starts at the wrong wall-clock minute, with no error and no signal.
evidence: app-next/src/domain/calendar.ts:32 — the loop breaks when the correction is zero
app-next/src/domain/calendar.ts:35 — otherwise the last guess is returned
app-next/src/domain/schedule.ts:14-20 — every window boundary flows through it
app-next/jest.config.js:7 — a 100% branch floor on src/domain that the default npm test does not run with --coverage
proposed_fix: Assert convergence (throw or clamp with a recorded diagnostic) rather than returning silently, and add a test for a half-hour-offset zone such as Australia/Adelaide and for Australia/Lord_Howe's 30-minute DST shift.
verifier_note: The unchecked return is real (app-next/src/domain/calendar.ts:18-35), and it is in fact the path that produces the spring-gap result — 02:30 on 2026-03-08 oscillates and falls out of the loop — which is deliberate and asserted at app-next/src/domain/__tests__/schedule.test.ts:40-41 and documented at app-next/src/domain/README.md:5. No failing case for a valid, unambiguous local time is demonstrated, so 'a window that starts at the wrong wall-clock minute' is speculative; the coverage-floor point (jest.config.js:8 vs package.json:45 'jest --runInBand') stands but is minor.

title: The minimum rule window is exactly 15 minutes — the same value as Apple's DeviceActivity floor, with zero margin
description: `validateRule` accepts any range where `(end - start + 1440) % 1440 >= 15`, and the time wheel steps in 5-minute increments, so a user can create a 15-minute blocking window. `DeviceActivityCenter` rejects intervals shorter than 15 minutes; a 15-minute window sits exactly on the boundary with no margin for how the adapter constructs `intervalStart`/`intervalEnd` DateComponents (inclusive vs exclusive end). If registration is rejected, that rule silently never blocks anything. P2-T04's schedule-generation tests cover weekday sets, cross-midnight and all-day but not the minimum-length case, and the 15-minute floor is not mentioned anywhere in the task.
proposed_fix: Raise the minimum window to 20 minutes (or 30, matching the 5-minute wheel), or keep 15 and add an explicit adapter test that a 15-minute window registers successfully on device before P2-T11 signs off. Whichever, state the reason next to the constant in `validateRule.ts` and in 01-product-model.md §2.
questions_for_johan: The builder currently lets a user create a 15-minute blocking window, which is exactly Apple's minimum DeviceActivity monitoring interval — no margin. Do you want to raise the minimum window to 20 or 30 minutes to keep clear of that floor, or keep 15 and accept that it must be proven on hardware in P2-T11?
verifier_note: The 15-minute floor is real (app-next/src/domain/validateRule.ts:73, picker steps of 5 at app-next/src/features/rules/TimeSheet.tsx:27) and P2-T04:39-41 lists weekday/cross-midnight/all-day schedule tests but no minimum-length case. However docs/research/device-activity-gaps.md:26 says DeviceActivityCenter rejects intervals *shorter* than 15 minutes, and plans/rebuild/01-product-model.md:81 states the 15-minute rule deliberately, so this is an untested boundary rather than a known defect.

title: After the camera-denied fallback the user is returned to a locked Home with no explanation
description: User experience: with the camera denied, the treadmill screen offers "Continue with phone in hand". Tapping it closes the screen and drops the user on Home, which still says "Apps are blocked" — because the handheld session starts in phase `verifying`, which `resolveLock` deliberately does not unlock. Nothing on Home says a walk is being verified or that they should keep walking. What the code says: the fallback calls `runtime.walking.start(rule)` and `router.back()` in the same handler, sets `verified.current = true` (suppressing the stop-on-unmount), and never opens the walking sheet. `resolveLock` excludes `verifying` from the unlock branch.
proposed_fix: After starting the handheld session, open the walking sheet on Home (or surface a `verifying` status line — "Checking your pace…") so the user sees the same "Start walking… / Checking your pace" state the sheet already has, rather than an unexplained locked card.
verifier_note: The handler at app-next/src/features/unlock/TreadmillUnlockScreen.tsx:111-118 does start the session and pop back, resolveLock.ts:16-22 unlocks only for phase walking|grace, and neither statusContent.ts:57-70 nor progressContent.ts:17-29 has any `verifying` copy — so the gap is real. But docs/specs/aha-unlock-screens.md:136-139 specifies exactly this dismissal, and the fake advances verifying→walking after one 6 s script step (WalkingFake.ts:21-28), so the locked Home is brief rather than an unexplained dead end.

title: An OS-restricted Location can never be represented, so Settings reports it as "Not requested"
description: User experience: on a device where Location is restricted by Screen Time content restrictions or an MDM profile, the app will store nothing usable — the store validator rejects `'restricted'` for `location` and keeps the previous value, so the Settings row reads "Not requested" and the permission detail offers to request a permission the OS will never grant. The user is told to allow something they cannot allow. What the code says: `permissionsStore` validates `location` against `['notDetermined','whenInUse','always','denied']` — no `restricted` — while every other permission uses `v.permission`, which includes it, and `settingsCopy.statuses` carries a `restricted` string that location can never reach.
proposed_fix: Add `'restricted'` to the location union in `permissionsStore` and `domain/types.ts`, and give restricted its own copy in `settingsCopy.without` explaining that a device restriction is in force and the app cannot request it.
verifier_note: app-next/src/state/permissionsStore.ts:18 omits 'restricted' from the location union (v.permission at app-next/src/state/validation.ts:15 includes it for every other permission), and app-next/src/content/settings.ts:87 carries a Restricted string location can never reach; the plan repeats the same union at plans/rebuild/01-product-model.md:208, so nothing schedules a fix. Real, but it only manifests on MDM/Screen-Time-restricted devices and yields a wrong label, not a broken lock.

title: The top-level Settings permission list omits Camera
description: User experience: a user whose treadmill scan stopped working goes to Settings, sees a "Permissions" group listing Screen Time, Motion & Fitness, Apple Health, Location and Notifications, and concludes the camera is not something ExcerLock uses. The Camera row exists only behind the "More settings" screen. Spec 02-screen-inventory.md:165 requires all six permission rows in Settings. What the code says: `permissionOrder` in `SettingsScreen.tsx` hard-codes five keys and drops `camera`; `DetailedSettingsScreen` iterates `Object.keys(settingsCopy.permissionNames)` and so does include it.
proposed_fix: Derive `permissionOrder` from `settingsCopy.permissionNames` so all six rows appear, or add `'camera'` explicitly. Also remove the duplicate "Notifications" row in the Preferences group (line 59), which navigates to the same detail screen already listed under Permissions.
verifier_note: app-next/src/features/settings/SettingsScreen.tsx:12 hard-codes five keys and omits `camera`, while app-next/src/content/settings.ts:62 defines a Camera name/why/without triplet and DetailedSettingsScreen.tsx:124-142 iterates all six. plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:165 requires Screen Time, Motion, Location, Health, Camera, Notifications rows in Settings, and the Preferences group at SettingsScreen.tsx:59 does duplicate the Notifications destination. Severity lowered: the row is still reachable one tap away behind "More settings", and camera matters only for treadmill scanning.

title: Nothing tells the user what signing in buys them or what skipping it costs
description: User experience: setup step X4 says "Save your progress / Keep your plan connected to you." and offers "Skip for now". Nothing states what is saved, what is lost by skipping, or that app selections can never move to a new phone (Apple ties Screen Time tokens to the device — decision 00-decisions.md:64). Signing in changes nothing observable, and the privacy copy actively contradicts the plan: "Your conditions and progress remain on this device" is false once Phase 2 syncs rules and rule_days. Signing out shows no confirmation and no note about what it does. What the code says: `SyncFake` is a total no-op — `pushRules`, `pushRuleDays` and `pull` all return empty — and grep finds no call sites for any of them.
proposed_fix: Add a benefit/consequence line to X4 and the Settings sign-in row: "Signing in restores your conditions and progress on a new phone. Your blocked-app selection stays on this device." Fix the privacy section to describe sync accurately. Add a short confirmation on sign-out stating that conditions and progress stay on this device.
verifier_note: Real part: app-next/src/content/setup.ts:35-36 is the only sign-in copy and never mentions that decision D5 (plans/rebuild/00-decisions.md:64) forbids app selections from syncing, and AccountScreen.tsx:59-62 signs out with no confirmation. Refuted parts: app-next/src/content/legal.ts:1 marks the privacy text as a Phase 1 placeholder to be replaced by counsel, and its line 16 is scoped to sign-out/deletion rather than a false sync claim; SyncFake being a no-op is exactly what plans/rebuild/phase-2-backend/P2-T08-sync.md schedules.

title: Pressing Edit on the plan summary can silently break Cancel, so Back keeps the change instead of discarding it
description: User experience: a user who explored more than one activity in onboarding (so `answers` has accumulated walking, gym, running and biking keys) presses Edit on the plan summary, changes the goal, then presses Back to cancel. The change is kept instead of reverted, with no message. What the code says: `edit()` writes `editBackup: JSON.stringify(answers)` into `answers`; the store's `answers` validator caps every string value at 500 characters and rejects the whole object if any value fails, so the patch is dropped entirely and neither `returnTo` nor `editBackup` is stored. `router.setParams({returnTo:'S3'})` still succeeds, so `back()` finds the param, fails to parse the missing backup, and restores the *current* (edited) answers. I measured a realistic multi-branch answer set at 664 characters — well over the limit; a single-branch set is 425–456.
proposed_fix: Stop round-tripping the snapshot through the validated `answers` map. Hold `editBackup` in component state (or a separate unvalidated store key with no length cap), and make `back()` fail loudly — keep the user on the edit step with an inline message — rather than silently restoring the edited values when no snapshot is found.
verifier_note: edit() at app-next/src/features/onboarding/useOnboarding.ts:52-58 stores the snapshot inside `answers`, whose validator (onboardingStore.ts:15 with validation.ts:3) rejects any value over 500 chars and, via createPersistedStore.ts:11-15, drops the whole `answers` field, while router.setParams still sets returnTo — so back() at useOnboarding.ts:59-72 falls into its catch and restores the edited answers. I measured a four-branch answer set at 502 chars before ruleId/ruleCreatedAt are added (619 after), so it is reachable, and the S3 Edit control is wired at OnboardingRoute.tsx:44. Severity lowered because it needs a user who explored three or four activity branches.

title: Starting a walk can fail with no error surface at all
description: User experience: the user taps "Start walking" in the walking sheet. If the start rejects — the condition was paused or deleted in another tab, or the mode is not `state` — the spinner stops and absolutely nothing else happens. No message, no state change, no retry hint. The rejection is an unhandled promise. What the code says: `WalkingSheet.start()` awaits `runtime.walking.start(rule)` inside a `try/finally` with no `catch`, and `WalkingFake.start` throws `'An enabled walking state condition is required'` for exactly those cases. The sheet has no error slot.
evidence: app-next/src/features/sessions/WalkingSheet.tsx:26-33 (try/finally with no catch and no error state)
app-next/src/demo/fakes/WalkingFake.ts:46-47 (start throws for a non-state or disabled rule)
app-next/src/features/unlock/TreadmillUnlockScreen.tsx:139 (the equivalent screen does render an alert label)
proposed_fix: Add a `catch` that sets an error string and render it as a `Label accessibilityRole="alert"` in the sheet, with a `sessionCopy.startError` key ("Couldn't start the walk. Check that this condition is on and scheduled now.").
also_titled: A live walking session has no error surface — a rejected start leaves the sheet looking idle
verifier_note: The missing catch is real: WalkingSheet.tsx:26-33 awaits runtime.walking.start in try/finally with no error state, and WalkingFake.ts:46-47 throws for a disabled or non-state rule. But the described entry states are unreachable: HomeSheets.tsx:13 only mounts the sheet for a rule that is `enabled` and still present, and progressContent.ts:27 emits action 'walk' only for state rules (treadmill ones route to /unlock at HomeScreen.tsx:102-103), so only a tight race can trigger it in Phase 1.

title: O03 advertises "Cycling" and "Strength training" as the app's activities; two screens later it offers Biking and Gym
description: The third intro screen shows four activity tiles labelled Walking, Running, Cycling, Strength training. The product has exactly four activities - Walking, Gym, Running, Biking - and O20 presents them under those names. A user primed for "Strength training" is then asked to pick "Gym", and one primed for "Cycling" gets "Biking". Two different vocabularies for the same four things, six screens apart.
proposed_fix: Change welcomeCopy.activities to ['Walking', 'Gym', 'Running', 'Biking'] so the intro names match the picker.
verifier_note: welcome.ts:7 does hold ['Walking','Running','Cycling','Strength training'] against the product's Walking/Gym/Running/Biking (activities.ts:2-5, 00-decisions.md:31), but ActivityTile.tsx:43 uses those strings only as the icon's accessibility label — the tiles render icon-only, so no sighted user ever reads 'Cycling' or 'Strength training'. Real vocabulary inconsistency, but it reaches VoiceOver users only.

title: The shield preview's `locked` and `lockWindow` causes produce byte-identical output
description: The dev-menu shield preview offers a three-way cause selector (locked, lockWindow, walkingEnded) but only two distinct screens exist: `shieldContent` consults `cause` solely to test for `'walkingEnded'`, so `locked` and `lockWindow` fall through the identical hint-based branch. The architecture plan explicitly reduces the old four shield causes to these three, so three distinct variants are the promise; the preview whose whole purpose is to get shield copy approved before the Swift is ported cannot show one of them. Compounding this, the preview passes a hint only when the live decision is `locked`, so in any other scenario both non-walking causes collapse to the generic fallback string.
proposed_fix: Give `lockWindow` its own subtitle (the window-start framing the old app used, e.g. "Blocking is on until 9 PM") or drop the third option from the selector and from the cause union.
questions_for_johan: What should the shield say when the cause is `lockWindow` rather than a generic `locked`? Right now the two are identical, so one of the three approved shield variants has no copy.
verifier_note: shieldContent.ts:3-15 branches only on cause === 'walkingEnded', so 'locked' and 'lockWindow' take the identical hint path, yet plans/rebuild/04-architecture.md:127 keeps three causes and ShieldPreview.tsx:9-11 offers all three in the selector while passing a hint only when the live decision is 'locked'. Severity lowered: the preview is dev-menu only in Phase 1, so the cost is an unapproved shield variant rather than a user-visible defect.

title: Starting a walk before the window opens burns the lease and unlocks nothing
description: Before the blocking window opens, Home still renders the rule's progress card with a "Start a walk" button. Tapping it creates a real session with a 15-minute lease and the sheet shows a live countdown and "Your apps are open while you walk" — but `resolveLock` requires the session's rule to be in-window, so nothing unlocks (nothing needed unlocking yet), and by the time the window opens the lease has partly or fully expired. The user's honest walk buys them nothing and the UI never says why.
evidence: app-next/src/domain/resolveLock.ts:15,20 (unlockedWalking requires the rule to be in `active`)
app-next/src/features/home/HomeScreen.tsx:90-108 (condition cards, with their actions, render in beforeWindow too)
app-next/src/features/home/progressContent.ts:17-29 (label 'Start a walk' regardless of window state)
app-next/src/content/sessions.ts (walkingBody: "Your apps are open while you walk.")
proposed_fix: Disable the start action outside the rule's window with an explanatory detail ("Starts at 9 AM"), or accept the start and hold the lease until the window opens. Either way the sheet must not claim the apps are open when they were never closed.
verifier_note: The mechanism is real: useTodayProgress (selectors.ts:42) yields today's instance before the window so HomeScreen.tsx:90-108 renders 'Start a walk' (progressContent.ts:17-29), and resolveLock.ts:16-21 only grants unlockedWalking when the rule is active. But nothing is 'burned' — state rules bank no credit by design, apps genuinely are open in beforeWindow so sessions.ts:6 is not false, and a walk continuing into the window does unlock; the surviving gap is only the missing 'starts at 9 AM' explanation next to the getAhead invitation (statusContent.ts:70-76).

title: Sign-out is silent and unconfirmed
description: `AccountScreen.tsx:60` calls `action(false)`, which awaits `signOut()` and sets no note — the heading support text quietly changes to 'anonymous'. There is no confirmation dialog and no statement about what leaves the device, in contrast to deletion which has a confirmation sheet with facts (`:33-46`). Given that Phase 2 sync (`P2-T08`) will make signing out consequential, a silent sign-out invites accidental data loss.
proposed_fix: Add a confirmation sheet for sign-out stating what stays on the device and what stops syncing, and a success note after it completes.
verifier_note: AccountScreen.tsx:20-21,60 does call `action(false)` with no confirmation and sets no note, unlike the delete path at :33-46 — that part holds. The data-loss rationale does not: P2-T10-settings-account-wiring.md:6 keeps local rules on the device (local-first) and P2-T08-sync.md:5-12 makes sync a backup/restore channel with pull only on sign-in, so signing out loses nothing.

title: 'Notifications' preference row opens the OS permission detail, not notification preferences
description: Under the heading 'Preferences', the 'Notifications' row navigates to `permission/notifications` (`SettingsScreen.tsx:59`), which is the permission-status explainer with an inert 'Open Settings' button (`PermissionDetail.tsx:22-31`). There is no way to control the two local notifications B14 defines (trial reminder, walk-lease warning) independently — a user who wants the lease warning but not the trial reminder, or vice versa, must turn all notifications off at the OS level. `plans/rebuild/00-decisions.md:35` names two distinct notifications but no screen exposes them.
proposed_fix: Either give the row per-notification toggles that gate scheduling, or rename it 'Notification permission' and move it into the Permissions group.
questions_for_johan: Should the two local notifications be individually toggleable in Settings, or is the OS-level permission the only control for v1?
verifier_note: The claimed gap is refuted: plans/rebuild/phase-2-backend/P2-T09-notifications.md:11 says the lease warning has "no toggle" and :12 says the permission is requested only from T3 and Settings › Permissions, and the spec's Preferences list (plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:166) contains no notification toggles. What is real is smaller — SettingsScreen.tsx:12 already renders a Notifications row inside the Permissions group, so the row at :59 is a second, misfiled entry to the identical route.

title: Home hides 'Add condition' exactly when a lock card is showing
description: Both `conditionCards` and the 'Add condition' button are gated on `!scheduleCard`, so on any locked or met day — the days a user is most likely to think 'I should add another way to unlock this' — the primary add affordance disappears, leaving only the small tertiary 'Edit / Add' link in the duplicate list header. On the Friday-met weekend carry-over day, a lock card renders with `progress.length === 0`, so neither the list header nor the add button renders and there is no route to add a condition from Home at all.
proposed_fix: Always render the add affordance on Home regardless of lock state.
verifier_note: conditionCards are not hidden — HomeScreen.tsx:172 renders them inside BlockingScheduleCard whenever scheduleCard exists, and app-next/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx:14-36 keeps a Conditions tab one tap away, so "no route to add a condition" is overstated. Real residue: the add shortcut at HomeScreen.tsx:277 is gated on !scheduleCard while plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:128 requires an "Add condition" shortcut on Home unconditionally.

title: The analytics streak ignores the selected period and always shows the lifetime figure
description: A user paging back to a previous week or month sees this week's streak number, unchanged, next to that period's other stats — the streak is computed over the whole history against today regardless of the selected period and offset.
evidence: app-next/src/features/analytics/analyticsModel.ts:53 — streak: streak(history, today), with no period or offset applied
app-next/src/domain/streak.ts:12-21 — streak() walks back from the day it is given
proposed_fix: Either compute the streak as of the last day of the selected period, or label it explicitly as a current lifetime streak and move it out of the period-scoped block.
verifier_note: The mechanism is as described (analyticsModel.ts:53 passes `today`, streak.ts:12-21 walks back from it), but the spec asks for exactly this: plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:154 lists "Days met ... current and longest streak" as one tile row, and the tile labels (AnalyticsScreen.tsx:128,134) say "{n}-day streak" / "Best: N days", never claiming a period. Minor ambiguity, not wrong behaviour.

title: unlockedMet.relockAt: null, afterWindow.nextLockAt: null and the copy that renders them are unreachable
description: `nextInstanceStart` scans an 8-day horizon and every schedule repeats weekly, so it can only return null when the enabled rule set is empty — a case in which the met branch's `enabled.find` already fails and the afterWindow branch's "a window ended today" test is also false. Both nullable fields, and `homeCopy.noNext` ("Your apps stay open until your next scheduled condition.") which is the only thing that renders them, are therefore dead. Harmless today, but it means the "permanent unlock" branch has never been reasoned about or tested, and a future change to the horizon or to schedule kinds would silently activate it.
proposed_fix: Either drop the nullability from `LockDecision` (types.ts:97, :99) and delete `homeCopy.noNext`, or add the test that proves the null path is reachable and correct. Whichever, say in `domain/README.md` which it is, because the enforcement adapter has to know whether a shield can ever be cleared indefinitely.
verifier_note: Both null branches are unreachable: reaching resolveLock.ts:31 requires an enabled rule with a windowInstance on row.day, and reaching :49's afterWindow requires a window that ended today, so in each case that rule recurs within nextInstanceStart's 8-day horizon (schedule.ts:32-37) and cannot return null. homeCopy.noNext (content/home.ts:34) is therefore rendered nowhere — statusContent.ts:32 is its only reader — and no test covers the null path (domain/__tests__/resolveLock.test.ts:110 only guards the non-null case).

title: Analytics reintroduces time-bank vocabulary the decision register cut
description: The per-activity section on Analytics is headed "How you earned time". Decision B1 removed the time bank entirely - no allowance, no earned minutes, no rate - and the surviving model is a single binary consequence: a met rule opens the apps for the rest of the day. Nothing is earned, so the heading describes a product that no longer exists and will confuse anyone reading the rest of the copy, which is consistently framed around unlocking rather than banking. The string is also a hardcoded literal outside src/content, while the content file's own heading for this section (`analyticsCopy.exercise` = "Your movement") is unused.
proposed_fix: Use `analyticsCopy.exercise` ("Your movement") for the heading and move any remaining literals into src/content/analytics.ts.
also_titled: Analytics reintroduces time-bank language that decision B1 cut
verifier_note: AnalyticsScreen.tsx:138 hardcodes the heading "How you earned time" over per-activity totals, while B1 (plans/rebuild/00-decisions.md:22) removes the time bank and "earned minutes" entirely; the surviving model is a met rule opening the apps. The content file's own heading for that section, analyticsCopy.exercise = "Your movement" (content/analytics.ts:15), is unused — the only `c.exercise` reference is TrendHero.tsx:35, which reads onboardingLabels, not analyticsCopy.

title: WalkingSheet's treadmill camera-preview placeholder is unreachable dead UI
description: `WalkingSheet` contains a mint-bordered square reading "Prop your phone on the console / Keep your full body in view. The camera preview appears here when connected", gated on `rule.mode.place === 'treadmill'`, and it also disables the Start button until framing is ready. That block can never render: `unlockKind` sends every state walking rule whose place is not `outside` to /unlock/treadmill, so the sheet is only ever opened for outdoor rules - which the aha spec confirms is now its only job. The result is a bordered placeholder promising a camera preview inside a sheet that has no camera path at all.
proposed_fix: Remove the treadmill framing block and the `frame.ready` gate from WalkingSheet, and delete the now-unused framing copy.
verifier_note: HomeScreen.tsx:102-104 opens the walk sheet only when unlockKind(rule) is null, and unlock/entry.ts:4 routes every non-outdoor state rule to /unlock/treadmill, so the treadmill block at WalkingSheet.tsx:109-127 (and the frame.ready gate at :57) can never render; HomeSheets.tsx:14 is the sole non-test mount. docs/specs/aha-unlock-screens.md:50-51 confirms WalkingSheet now serves outdoor state rules only, superseding the older SH-walk placeholder note.

title: An overnight gym rule replays the arrival ceremony after midnight
description: With an overnight gym window (e.g. 20:00–02:00), a user who checked in at 23:30 and re-opens the gym unlock screen at 00:30 gets the full ceremony again — ring, shackle lift, confetti — for an arrival that was already credited. `alreadyCredited` looks the met row up under `dayKey(now)`, but progress rows for a cross-midnight instance are keyed to the day the window *starts* on, so after midnight the lookup misses and the screen believes nothing has been booked. The suppression path (`celebrate={false}`) that exists precisely for this case never engages.
evidence: app-next/src/demo/gymProgress.ts:36 and app-next/src/demo/fakes/GymFake.ts:73-75 (rows written against currentInstances(...)[0].day — the window's start day)
app-next/src/domain/schedule.ts:13,15 (a cross-midnight instance keeps the day it starts on)
docs/specs/aha-unlock-screens.md:197-199 (an already-credited arrival should show the lifted state directly — no ring, no confetti)
proposed_fix: Resolve the row the same way the writers do — `currentInstances(rule, now, tz)[0]?.day ?? dayKey(now, tz)` — instead of `dayKey(now, tz)`.
verifier_note: GymUnlockScreen.tsx:20-24 looks the met row up under dayKey(now), while both writers key rows to the window's start day — demo/gymProgress.ts:36 and demo/fakes/GymFake.ts:73-75 use currentInstances(...)[0]?.day ?? dayKey(now) — and schedule.ts:15 keeps a cross-midnight instance on its start day. Overnight windows are a real, labelled feature (domain/types.ts:32, scheduleLabel.ts:17 "ends next day"), so after midnight alreadyCredited is false and the ceremony replays.

title: Duplicate Account row in the detail settings screen
description: The detail screen shows an Account row in the 'General' group at `DetailedSettingsScreen.tsx:99-104` and a second one, same destination, in the 'Other' group at `:168`. The compact top-level screen also has one (`SettingsScreen.tsx:25-30`). Three entry points to the same screen on two levels reads as an oversight and makes the specified Settings ordering (`plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:159-171`) harder to verify.
proposed_fix: Keep the profile/account row once, at the top, matching the screen inventory.
verifier_note: The two rows are real (DetailedSettingsScreen.tsx:99-104 and :168 both navigate('account')), but the screen inventory itself lists both a "Profile header: name, sign-in state" and a separate "Account: Sign in / Sign out, Delete account" entry (plans/rebuild/02-screen-inventory.md:159,168-169), so this is closer to a literal reading of the spec than an oversight; the compact screen's row (SettingsScreen.tsx:25-30) is on a different screen, not a third row on the same one.
